correctness.rationale: Block-determinant quartic and exact two-dimensional Routh–Hurwitz inequality yield a unique angular threshold for all positive parameter quadruples. At equality the polynomial factors into one imaginary and one decaying quadratic, and the crossing speed is nonzero; beyond the threshold the system has a positive-real-part eigenvalue. Symbolic identities and 6000 sampled state spectra were verified from the included checker. Finite samples are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result is a sharp iff classification and explicit oscillatory counterexample to assuming inertia preserves the noninertial angular tolerance. These conclusions cannot be recovered by logical implication from the checked earlier stability guarantees.

evidence: The 2023 paper analyzes the exact-eigenvector linearization; its scalar damped modes are diagonalizable and do not include a fixed rotated eigenspace.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A projector orientation error produces a nonsymmetric reflected Hessian with a complex-conjugate spectral pair; after adding inertia this pair can become unstable even when the first-order reflected flow remains stable. Exact-basis heavy-ball equivalence is therefore inapplicable.

Targeted scholarly searches and direct comparison of the closest full texts found no same statement; unindexed priority remains possible.

The novelty assertion concerns the application-specific sharp classification, not the classical Routh–Hurwitz test or parabolic stability of damped matrix modes.

value.rationale: Provides a motivated exact fidelity threshold in a standard accelerated saddle-search model, with an open instability wedge despite exponential convergence of its first-order analogue and an explicit unit-curvature witness. Separates two natural spectral transitions and yields design guidance not available from a generic sufficiency estimate; scope is honestly restricted to a fixed planar projector.
